account: Maria Ilyas, Rehan Ahmed Khan and colleagues ran a randomized crossover trial from February to July 2024 with 100 fourth-year medical students in the general surgery course at Islamic International Medical College, Riphah International University, Pakistan. After a pre-test, one group of 50 studied the acute abdomen topic for two hours through personalized learning pathways that ChatGPT-4 produced from standard prompts and from a form on each student's study habits. The other group of 50 used conventional resources for the same time. Pre-test scores did not differ significantly, 17.12 in the ChatGPT-4 group and 18.64 in the control group. On the first post-test, the ChatGPT-4 group scored 22.8 against 19.24 (p = 0.005, Cohen's d = 0.58). The groups then switched methods for one more hour, and the scores on a second post-test were similar. The authors note that the trial took place at a single institution on one surgical topic and measured short-term performance, and that it had no formal washout period between phases. The Pakistan Journal of Medical Sciences published the study in August 2026.
